feed.title: Implicit Deletions and Improvements in Utreexo IBD

entry.title: Implicit Deletions and Improvements in Utreexo IBD
entry.summary:
SwiftSync enables consensus over the UTXO set without imposing constraints on its structure. This flexibility raises the possibility of representing the UTXO set as a utreexo accumulator, which is appealing due to SwiftSync's superior performance during initial block download (IBD) compared to utreexo's IBD process that requires proof branches. Despite this efficiency, there remains a need for a compact UTXO representation, such as the utreexo accumulator, once synchronization reaches the blockchain tip.
By attaching position data to each UTXO—that is, incrementally numbering every transaction output (TXO) and retaining this number—it becomes feasible to hash the resulting set directly into a utreexo accumulator. The structure of the utreexo tree depends exclusively on the sequence of spent TXOs, which can be deduced from these positional numbers. For instance, if UTXOs are found at positions 2 and 5, it is evident that positions 3 and 4 have already been spent.
Instead of conducting SwiftSync to track positional data and subsequently converting the synchronized UTXO set into a utreexo accumulator, both operations can be integrated and executed simultaneously. The SwiftSync hints file inherently provides the necessary position data, allowing the transition to begin immediately rather than waiting for IBD completion.
Block processing order, while theoretically flexible, does not require arbitrary sequencing in practical implementations. Processing blocks after accumulating a sequential range does not introduce delays but rather brings advantages such as reduced state requirements, improved caching efficiency, and simpler wallet scanning throughout IBD. Additional insights on validation order can be found in [this resource](https://gist.github.com/RubenSomsen/21c45b1c57448881ce5007d884fb3f21order-of-validation).
